Of the epic form ἀσχαλάω [I am distressed] there is one example among the tragedians, Eur. Iph. A. 920, where at the end of the trimeter τοῖς κακοῖσί τ᾽ ἀσχα-λᾶν [and to be distressed at the evils], if these verses were written by Euripides. Therefore L. Dindorf seems rightly to have restored ξυνασχαλεῖ [he grieves with] in Prometheus verses 161 and 243 in Thes. vol. 1, 2 p. 2320, and there at v. 754 with Herwerden ἀσχαλεῖ [he is distressed] for ἀσχαλᾷ [he is distressed].
